# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog
          # and same-version pack zips (version uniqueness + payload compare).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          # gh-812: base versions come from what the last release SHIPPED —
          # versions.json on main is a best-effort ledger that can (and did)
          # lag reality by whole releases, re-shipping a live version with
          # new content.
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (guard 1), wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch, re-run
        # the guard (guard 2), and CLOSE the PR when the diff went empty.
        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is
        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
        # publishing.
        if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          origin_url="https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
          git remote set-url origin "$origin_url"
          # Commit FIRST (compile rewrote versions.json — unstaged tracked
          # files make later operations refuse).
          git add versions.json
          git diff --cache…

Now, let me deep-review the code for issues.

## Analysis of ci/pack_require_gate.cjs

1. `REQUIRE_RE = /\brequire\s*\(\s*(['"])((?:\.\.?\/)[^'"]*)\1\s*\)/g`

Issues:
- `\brequire` will match `.require(...)`, e.g. `foo.require('./x')` — matches `require` in `mod.require(...)`. This is actually a member-call like `module.require`, which is fine (that's a real require). But it would also match text in comments and strings (documented limitation — comments not stripped, documented in header as a decision). OK.
- The regex captures `require` word but a preceding `.` satisfies `\b` (e.g., `foo.require('./a.js')` — `\b` between `.` and `require` exists since `.` is a non-word char). Fine.
- It doesn't match `require\s*\(\s*(['"])...` where spec starts with `./` or `../`. What about a spec like `'.'`? Not relevant.
- Nested quotes: spec content `[^'"]*` stops at either quote — a spec containing an apostrophe would break, but paths don't have apostrophes typically.
- Note: `require ("../b/c.js")` is matched due to `\s*` — fine.

2. `requireSpecs` — fresh regex per call, good (avoids lastIndex issue).

3. `resolveRequire` — fromPath.split('/'), pop the file name... comment says "the requiring file's directory" but `pop()` removes the FILE NAME (last segment), leaving the directory. The comment is slightly wrong ("parts.pop(); // the requiring file's directory" — actually pops the file name, leaving the directory). Minor comment nit.

4. `normalizePath` — pops on '..' — if `out` is empty, `out.pop()` returns undefined, fine. A spec like `'../../../etc/passwd'` would climb out of zip root — but membership test would then check 'etc/passwd' which is not in the zip. No security issue (read-only classification).

5. `resolveRequireCandidates` — for spec starting with './', adds js/-root-relative candidate. But NOT for spec starting with '../'. Documented.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 813
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/813
- **Title**: gh-812 [BUG] Pack release shipped sm_github-0.1.36.zip twice with different content — 091304 pack missing reviewVerdicts.js, all fa ticks red (rollback pinned to 075526)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-812` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +1007
- **Deletions**: -22
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T10:49:43Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T10:49:43Z

## PR Description

Closes #812
### Root Cause

The pack-release pipeline derived pack versions from `versions.json` on main — a ledger whose push back is best-effort and never landed (a rejected direct push only warns). Evidence: 8 consecutive releases (20261008-095538 → 20261009-091304) all advertised `sm_github: 0.1.36` while content changed; the 091304 release republished a **different** `sm_github-0.1.36.zip` (sha256 `20352463…`) than the 075526 release (`0dc62ca4…`). Version-keyed consumer caches then ran mixed content — post-#810 code requiring `./reviewVerdicts.js` over an installed 0.1.36 tree without it — and every fa machine-sm tick went red. Verified against the artifacts: both zips are internally self-consistent; the collision (not a missing file in the new zip) is the defect. No sanity gate existed: `validatePack()` only re-hashes manifest entries against themselves.

### Fix

- `ci/pack_version_guard.cjs` (new): base version prefers the **previous release's shipped catalog** (append-only, can't be rewritten by a failed push) over the ledger; a rebuilt-but-unbumped agent whose payload differs from what its version already shipped gets an extra patch bump. Fingerprint = manifest `files` (path+sha256) only — `sourceCommit`/version metadata never counts as content change.
- `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs` (new): release self-test — every literal relative `require` in every packed `.js` must resolve inside the zip (file-relative **or** `js/`-root-relative base; dmtools resolves both). Unresolved → the release fails (exit ≠ 0) before ledger commit and publish.
- `ci/release_packs.mjs`: wires both (`--prev-release-tag`, payload-drift re-version, gate after the launch augment, before validate).
- `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml`: passes the previous release tag + `GH_TOKEN` to the build step.
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md`: release-integrity contract + the rollback contract (pin `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`/`AGENTS_VERSION` to an `agents-rel-<tag>` base URL — the live mitigation).

### Test Coverage

- New suites: `test_packRequireGate.js` (20 tests, incl. the L2 red-team mixed-content fixture that must FAIL), `test_packVersionGuard.js` (15 tests, incl. the incident replay asserting 091304 would ship 0.1.37), +7 wiring tests in `test_releasePacks.js`.
- Live rehearsal on the real artifacts: full builder run vs the 075526 release — `sm_github` shipped **0.1.37**, 61/68 agents kept their version with byte-identical payloads, **0 version collisions** fleet-wide; tampered zip (file removed) → gate exit 1; missing require → `dmtools compile` fails the release (exit 1) on the current CLI.

# gh-812: [BUG] Pack release shipped sm_github-0.1.36.zip twice with different content — 091304 pack missing reviewVerdicts.js, all fa ticks red (rollback pinned to 075526)

## Description

## Goal

The pack release pipeline must never publish two different packs under the same version number: every release that changes pack content bumps the pack version (or names artifacts content-addressed), and the pack zip must include every JS file the packed code requires.

## Subject

`agent-pack-release.yml` / pack build for `sm_github` (and sibling packs). Live incident 2026-10-09: PR #810 added code that `require('./reviewVerdicts.js')`, the release `agents-rel-20261009-091304` shipped **sm_github-0.1.36.zip WITHOUT that file** — the same version number as the previous working pack (from `agents-rel-20261009-075526`). Every fa machine-sm tick failed for ~25 min (`❌ Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js ... /home/runner/.dmtools/packs/sm_github-0.1.36/js/reviewVerdicts.js`); mitigation = repointing `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY` + `AGENTS_VERSION` to 075526.

## Capability surface

- Pack build input: all `js/` sources of the pack directory (glob, not a hand-maintained manifest) — a new file can never be forgotten.
- Version: pack version must change whenever pack content changes (auto-bump from release tag timestamp, or content hash in the artifact name).
- Release sanity gate: after upload, download the pack zip back and assert every `require('./x')` target inside pack JS resolves to a file in the zip (self-test before publish).
- Rollback contract: registry consumers must be able to pin `<release-tag>` base URL (already used in the incident) — document it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: a PR adding `foo.js` + a require of it, merged with the pipeline, produces a pack zip CONTAINING `foo.js` (pipeline self-test green).
2. AC2: two releases with differing pack content never share a version string (test: build twice with a change, assert different artifact name/version).
3. AC3: release self-test fails the release (exit != 0) when a require target is missing from the zip.
4. AC4: rerunning the fa tick on the fixed release resolves all requires (verified live in fa).

## Test plan

- L1: pack-build unit tests (glob completeness, version bump).
- L2: replay the 091304 content set — self-test must FAIL it (red team the gate).
- L3 (live): next real merge produces a bumped pack and fa ticks go green on `latest` unpinned.

## Non-goals

- Changing fa/dmtools-dart installer caching behavior (separate issue in dmtools-dart).
- Renaming existing historical artifacts.

## References

- Incident: fa run 37914059566 (job 113765858088), ticks red 09:36–09:52Z 2026-10-09; mitigation pins in fa vars (`AGENTS_VERSION`, `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY` → 075526).
- Source PR: #810 (verdict reconciliation — legitimate code, bad packaging).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instruction…

# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog
          # and same-version pack zips (version uniqueness + payload compare).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          # gh-812: base versions come from what the last release SHIPPED —
          # versions.json on main is a best-effort ledger that can (and did)
          # lag reality by whole releases, re-shipping a live version with
          # new content.
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (guard 1), wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch, re-run
        # the guard (guard 2), and CLOSE the PR when the diff went empty.
        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is
        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
        # publishing.
        if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          origin_url="https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
          git remote set-url origin "$origin_url"
          # Commit FIRST (compile rewrote versions.json — unstaged tracked
          # files make later operations refuse).
          git add versions.json
          git diff --cache…

+### Pack release integrity (gh-812) and the rollback contract
+
+Two releases with differing pack content must never share a version
+string. Live 2026-10-09 (gh-812): the version ledger (`versions.json`)
+push back to main is best-effort and never landed, so consecutive
+releases recomputed the same bump and shipped two different
+`sm_github-0.1.36.zip` files (075526 vs 091304); version-keyed consumer
+caches ran mixed content and every fa machine-sm tick went red for
+~25 min. The pipeline now guarantees:
+
+- **Shipped-version-first base** — `ci/release_packs.mjs` reads each
+  agent's base version from the PREVIOUS release's `catalog.json`
+  (append-only release history; `--prev-release-tag`), falling back to
+  `versions.json` only when the release/`gh` is unavailable. A failed
+  ledger push can no longer make a release reuse a version that is
+  already out there.
+- **Payload-drift re-versioning** — a rebuilt-but-unbumped agent whose
+  payload differs from the zip its version already shipped is re-versioned
+  one patch up (manifest `files` fingerprints; metadata like
+  `sourceCommit` never counts as a content change). Byte-identical
+  rebuilds keep their version — no churn.
+- **Require sanity gate** — every built zip is unpacked and every literal
+  relative `require` in every packed `.js` must resolve to a file inside
+  the zip (file-relative OR js/-root-relative base — dmtools resolves
+  both). Unresolved requires fail the release (exit != 0) before the
+  ledger commit and the publish. This is defense-in-depth on top of
+  `dmtools compile`'s own require-closure check of the repo sources: the
+  gate verifies the produced ARTIFACT, whatever CLI version built it.
+
+Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
+of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
+the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
+`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
+`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
+and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
+what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
+forward: content changes always produce a new version string.
+

- AC1: a PR adding `foo.js` + a require of it, merged with the pipeline, produces a pack zip CONTAING `foo.js` (pipeline self-test green). — the require gate asserts requires resolve inside the zip. Note that the gate asserts self-consistency of the zip; but if `dmtools compile` doesn't include the file, the gate fails. OK.
- AC2: two releases with differing pack content never share a version string — version guard + payload drift re-version.
- AC3: release self-test fails the release (exit != 0) when a require target is missing from the zip — assertZipRequires throws.
- AC4: rerunning the fa tick on the fixed release resolves all requires — live verification claimed.

Now, let me deep-review the code for issues.

## Analysis of ci/pack_require_gate.cjs

1. `REQUIRE_RE = /\brequire\s*\(\s*(['"])((?:\.\.?\/)[^'"]*)\1\s*\)/g`

Issues:
- `\brequire` will match `.require(...)`, e.g. `foo.require('./x')` — matches `require` in `mod.require(...)`. This is actually a member-call like `module.require`, which is fine (that's a real require). But it would also match text in comments and strings (documented limitation — comments not stripped, documented in header as a decision). OK.
- The regex captures `require` word but a preceding `.` satisfies `\b` (e.g., `foo.require('./a.js')` — `\b` between `.` and `require` exists since `.` is a non-word char). Fine.
- It doesn't match `require\s*\(\s*(['"])...` where spec starts with `./` or `../`. What about a spec like `'.'`? Not relevant.
- Nested quotes: spec content `[^'"]*` stops at either quote — a spec containing an apostrophe would break, but paths don't have apostrophes typically.
- Note: `require ("../b/c.js")` is matched due to `\s*` — fine.

2. `requireSpecs` — fresh regex per call, good (avoids lastIndex issue).

3. `resolveRequire` — fromPath.split('/'), pop the file name... comment says "the requiring file's directory" but `pop()` removes the FILE NAME (last segment), leaving the directory. The comment is slightly wrong ("parts.pop(); // the requiring file's directory" — actually pops the file name, leaving the directory). Minor comment nit.

4. `normalizePath` — pops on '..' — if `out` is empty, `out.pop()` returns undefined, fine. A spec like `'../../../etc/passwd'` would climb out of zip root — but membership test would then check 'etc/passwd' which is not in the zip. No security issue (read-only classification).

5. `resolveRequireCandidates` — for spec starting with './', adds js/-root-relative candidate. But NOT for spec starting with '../'. Documented.

6. `unresolvedRequires` — checks `pathSetHas(paths, bases[b]) || pathSetHas(paths, bases[b] + '.js')`. Note that `resolveRequire` doesn't append `.js` if the spec omits it (e.g. `require('./common/helper')`). The + '.js' check covers that. Good.

But wait — there's a subtle issue: the knownPaths default builds `{}` from files' own paths — only files passed in. In the builder, `assertZipRequires` passes the full zip walk `paths` Set — includes non-.js files too (e.g. `manifest.json`, `launch.json`). Good.

7. Potential false-negative: `.js` files inside zip whose content is `source` read as utf8 — fine.

8. A subtle issue: the gate scans ALL .js files in the zip including e.g. `verdict.sh`? No — only `.js`. Launch extras like `verdict.sh` are shell, ignored. OK.

9. What about requires in `.json` files? Not scanned. Agent configs may embed JS strings in JSON? Hmm — pack zips contain agent config JSONs which may contain inline JS? The gate only scans `.js`. This is a gap but likely fine given dmtools compile embeds closure.

## Analysis of ci/pack_version_guard.cjs

1. `bump()` — `parseInt(parts[0], 10) || 0`. Fine.

2. `payloadFingerprint` — uses `manifest.files` — path + sha256. What if `files[i].path` is undefined? Would create 'undefined:hash'. Minor.

3. `fingerprintsDiffer` — null-safe.

## Analysis of ci/release_packs.mjs

Key flows:

1. `shippedCatalog()`:
```js
if (!PREV_TAG || DRY_RUN) return {}; // no previous release to read — ledger fallback
SHIPPED_DIR = mkdtempSync(...);
try {
  execSync(`gh release download ...`);
  SHIPPED_CATALOG = JSON.parse(readFileSync(...));
} catch (e) {
  console.warn(`::warning::...`);
  rmSync(SHIPPED_DIR, ...);
  SHIPPED_DIR = null;
  SHIPPED_CATALOG = {};
}
```
- If catalog.json downloaded but JSON.parse throws → SHIPPED_DIR not cleaned in catch (rmSync is in catch, actually the catch does rmSync(SHIPPED_DIR) — yes it does; wait: the catch sets `SHIPPED_CATALOG = {}` and rmSync(SHIPPED_DIR). OK it cleans. Actually look: catch block: warn, rmSync(SHIPPED_DIR...), SHIPPED_DIR=null, SHIPPED_CATALOG={}. Good.

2. `shippedZipManifest(agent, version)`:
```js
if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(SHIPPED_ZIP_MANIFESTS, key)) return ...;
if (!PREV_TAG || DRY_RUN || !SHIPPED_DIR) return null;
```
- Note: `SHIPPED_DIR` may be null if shippedCatalog() failed or was never called. In main(), `shippedCatalog()` is always called before (via `const shippedVersion = shippedCatalog()[agent] || null;`). If PREV_TAG && !DRY_RUN and gh succeeded, SHIPPED_DIR is set. OK.
- BUT: there's a bug candidate — in `buildPackRelease`, the drift check is only performed when `!isAffected && shippedVersion === next`. For an affected agent, next = bump(shipped) — never equals shippedVersion, so no drift check needed (version already bumped). Fine.

Wait — actually there's a subtle issue: `shippedZipManifest` downloads `${agent}-${version}.zip` from the previous release. But what if the previous release shipped the agent at a DIFFERENT version than `shippedVersion` (catalog says 0.1.36 but the zip asset name)? They should match by construction.

Another subtle issue: `shippedZipManifest` caches `null` results. Fine.

3. **Cache-poisoning issue in SHIPPED_DIR**: `gh release download --pattern '${agent}-${version}.zip' --dir SHIPPED_DIR --clobber`. `--pattern` uses glob. The agent name could be a prefix of another agent's name! E.g. agents `sm` and `sm_github`: pattern `sm-0.1.36.zip` — glob `sm-0.1.36.zip` matches only exact name `sm-0.1.36.zip` (glob has no wildcard here), fine.

4. **The drift-check skip for dry-run**: in dry-run, `shippedZipManifest` returns null → fingerprintsDiffer(null, ...) = false → no re-version. Dry-run is not published, fine.

5. **Critical check — the drift re-version path**: 
```js
if (!isAffected && shippedVersion === next &&
    fingerprintsDiffer(shippedZipManifest(agent, shippedVersion), zipManifestText(zip))) {
  next = resolveShipVersion(next, true);
  ...rebuild, gate, validate, return
}
assertZipRequires(zip);
```
- Issue: when the drift check runs, `shippedZipManifest()` is called BEFORE `zipManifestText(zip)`? Arguments evaluated left-to-right: `fingerprintsDiffer(shippedZipManifest(...), zipManifestText(zip))` — left operand first. OK.
- Note: For an UNAFFECTED agent, next = shippedVersion (base = shipped since unaffected). So `shippedVersion === next` is true whenever the shipped catalog has the agent. So every unaffected agent downloads its previous zip and compares fingerprints. That's ~68 agents → 68 gh download calls per release (lazily only when shippedVersion === next — which is every unaffected agent). Performance concern: each release makes ~68 sequential `gh release download` + `unzip -p` exec calls. Acceptable? It's a release pipeline, one per push to main. The PR description says "61/68 agents kept their version with byte-identical payloads" — so it works. Could be slow but OK. Maybe a SUGGESTION about parallelism. Not critical.

- **More important**: If the previous release didn't include the agent's zip (e.g. older releases only shipped affected agents — historical releases before the "build every agent" rule), `shippedZipManifest` returns null with a `::warning::`. Fine, degrades.

6. **The `versions[agent] = next` ledger write**: In main loop, `versions[agent] = next` for ALL agents (not just affected). And ledgerChanged check: `agents.some((a) => versions[a] !== (ledgerBefore[a] || '0.1.0'))`. - **PR #**: 813
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/813
- **Title**: gh-812 [BUG] Pack release shipped sm_github-0.1.36.zip twice with different content — 091304 pack missing reviewVerdicts.js, all fa ticks red (rollback pinned to 075526)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-812` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +1007
- **Deletions**: -22
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T10:49:43Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T10:49:43Z

## PR Description

Closes #812
### Root Cause

The pack-release pipeline derived pack versions from `versions.json` on main — a ledger whose push back is best-effort and never landed (a rejected direct push only warns). Evidence: 8 consecutive releases (20261008-095538 → 20261009-091304) all advertised `sm_github: 0.1.36` while content changed; the 091304 release republished a **different** `sm_github-0.1.36.zip` (sha256 `20352463…`) than the 075526 release (`0dc62ca4…`). Version-keyed consumer caches then ran mixed content — post-#810 code requiring `./reviewVerdicts.js` over an installed 0.1.36 tree without it — and every fa machine-sm tick went red. Verified against the artifacts: both zips are internally self-consistent; the collision (not a missing file in the new zip) is the defect. No sanity gate existed: `validatePack()` only re-hashes manifest entries against themselves.

### Fix

- `ci/pack_version_guard.cjs` (new): base version prefers the **previous release's shipped catalog** (append-only, can't be rewritten by a failed push) over the ledger; a rebuilt-but-unbumped agent whose payload differs from what its version already shipped gets an extra patch bump. Fingerprint = manifest `files` (path+sha256) only — `sourceCommit`/version metadata never counts as content change.
- `ci/pack_require_gate.cjs` (new): release self-test — every literal relative `require` in every packed `.js` must resolve inside the zip (file-relative **or** `js/`-root-relative base; dmtools resolves both). Unresolved → the release fails (exit ≠ 0) before ledger commit and publish.
- `ci/release_packs.mjs`: wires both (`--prev-release-tag`, payload-drift re-version, gate after the launch augment, before validate).
- `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml`: passes the previous release tag + `GH_TOKEN` to the build step.
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md`: release-integrity contract + the rollback contract (pin `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`/`AGENTS_VERSION` to an `agents-rel-<tag>` base URL — the live mitigation).

### Test Coverage

- New suites: `test_packRequireGate.js` (20 tests, incl. the L2 red-team mixed-content fixture that must FAIL), `test_packVersionGuard.js` (15 tests, incl. the incident replay asserting 091304 would ship 0.1.37), +7 wiring tests in `test_releasePacks.js`.
- Live rehearsal on the real artifacts: full builder run vs the 075526 release — `sm_github` shipped **0.1.37**, 61/68 agents kept their version with byte-identical payloads, **0 version collisions** fleet-wide; tampered zip (file removed) → gate exit 1; missing require → `dmtools compile` fails the release (exit 1) on the current CLI.

### Notes

- Full suite: 2126 passed, 2 failed — both failures (`test_reviewVerdicts.js`, gh-807 round-3) reproduce on a clean tree with this diff stashed; pre-existing, untouched subsystem.
- The ticket's premise ("091304 zip missing reviewVerdicts.js") is contradicted by the artifacts — the published 091304 zip contains the file; RCA details the corrected chain. The requested gates are still built and red-team-verified.
- dmtools-dart installer caching and historical artifact renames untouched (non-goals).

# gh-812: [BUG] Pack release shipped sm_github-0.1.36.zip twice with different content — 091304 pack missing reviewVerdicts.js, all fa ticks red (rollback pinned to 075526)

## Description

## Goal

The pack release pipeline must never publish two different packs under the same version number: every release that changes pack content bumps the pack version (or names artifacts content-addressed), and the pack zip must include every JS file the packed code requires.

## Subject

`agent-pack-release.yml` / pack build for `sm_github` (and sibling packs). Live incident 2026-10-09: PR #810 added code that `require('./reviewVerdicts.js')`, the release `agents-rel-20261009-091304` shipped **sm_github-0.1.36.zip WITHOUT that file** — the same version number as the previous working pack (from `agents-rel-20261009-075526`). Every fa machine-sm tick failed for ~25 min (`❌ Failed to require module: ./reviewVerdicts.js ... /home/runner/.dmtools/packs/sm_github-0.1.36/js/reviewVerdicts.js`); mitigation = repointing `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY` + `AGENTS_VERSION` to 075526.

## Capability surface

- Pack build input: all `js/` sources of the pack directory (glob, not a hand-maintained manifest) — a new file can never be forgotten.
- Version: pack version must change whenever pack content changes (auto-bump from release tag timestamp, or content hash in the artifact name).
- Release sanity gate: after upload, download the pack zip back and assert every `require('./x')` target inside pack JS resolves to a file in the zip (self-test before publish).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
          # gh-812: the builder reads the previous release's shipped catalog
          # and same-version pack zips (version uniqueness + payload compare).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          # gh-812: base versions come from what the last release SHIPPED —
          # versions.json on main is a best-effort ledger that can (and did)
          # lag reality by whole releases, re-shipping a live version with
          # new content.
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--prev-release-tag="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (guard 1), wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch, re-run
        # the guard (guard 2), and CLOSE the PR when the diff went empty.
        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is
        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
        # publishing.
        if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          origin_url="https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
          git remote set-url origin "$origin_url"
          # Commit FIRST (compile rewrote versions.json — unstaged tracked
          # files make later operations refuse).
          git add versions.json
          git diff --cache…

+### Pack release integrity (gh-812) and the rollback contract
+
+Two releases with differing pack content must never share a version
+string. Live 2026-10-09 (gh-812): the version ledger (`versions.json`)
+push back to main is best-effort and never landed, so consecutive
+releases recomputed the same bump and shipped two different
+`sm_github-0.1.36.zip` files (075526 vs 091304); version-keyed consumer
+caches ran mixed content and every fa machine-sm tick went red for
+~25 min. The pipeline now guarantees:
+
+- **Shipped-version-first base** — `ci/release_packs.mjs` reads each
+  agent's base version from the PREVIOUS release's `catalog.json`
+  (append-only release history; `--prev-release-tag`), falling back to
+  `versions.json` only when the release/`gh` is unavailable. A failed
+  ledger push can no longer make a release reuse a version that is
+  already out there.
+- **Payload-drift re-versioning** — a rebuilt-but-unbumped agent whose
+  payload differs from the zip its version already shipped is re-versioned
+  one patch up (manifest `files` fingerprints; metadata like
+  `sourceCommit` never counts as a content change). Byte-identical
+  rebuilds keep their version — no churn.
+- **Require sanity gate** — every built zip is unpacked and every literal
+  relative `require` in every packed `.js` must resolve to a file inside
+  the zip (file-relative OR js/-root-relative base — dmtools resolves
+  both). Unresolved requires fail the release (exit != 0) before the
+  ledger commit and the publish. This is defense-in-depth on top of
+  `dmtools compile`'s own require-closure check of the repo sources: the
+  gate verifies the produced ARTIFACT, whatever CLI version built it.
+
+Rollback contract: registry consumers pin a release-tag base URL instead
+of `latest` — exactly the live mitigation used during the incident. Set
+the registry/base vars (`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`,
+`AGENTS_VERSION`) to the known-good tag, e.g.
+`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/agents-rel-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`,
+and the packs resolve from that release's assets + catalog regardless of
+what newer releases publish. Cut a fresh release (never re-tag) to move
+forward: content changes always produce a new version string.

Now let me check the ticket's ACs against the PR:

- AC1: a PR adding `foo.js` + a require of it, merged with the pipeline, produces a pack zip CONTAING `foo.js` (pipeline self-test green). — the require gate asserts requires resolve inside the zip. Note that the gate asserts self-consistency of the zip; but if `dmtools compile` doesn't include the file, the gate fails. OK.
- AC2: two releases with differing pack content never share a version string — version guard + payload drift re-version.
- AC3: release self-test fails the release (exit != 0) when a require target is missing from the zip — assertZipRequires throws.
- AC4: rerunning the fa tick on the fixed release resolves all requires — live verification claimed.

Now, let me deep-review the code for issues.

## Analysis of ci/pack_require_gate.cjs

1. `REQUIRE_RE = /\brequire\s*\(\s*(['"])((?:\.\.?\/)[^'"]*)\1\s*\)/g`

Issues:
- `\brequire` will match `.require(...)`, e.g. `foo.require('./x')` — matches `require` in `mod.require(...)`. This is actually a member-call like `module.require`, which is fine (that's a real require). But it would also match text in comments and strings (documented limitation — comments not stripped, documented in header as a decision). OK.
- The regex captures `require` word but a preceding `.` satisfies `\b` (e.g., `foo.require('./a.js')` — `\b` between `.` and `require` exists since `.` is a non-word char). Fine.
- It doesn't match `require\s*\(\s*(['"])...` where spec starts with `./` or `../`. What about a spec like `'.'`? Not relevant.
- Nested quotes: spec content `[^'"]*` stops at either quote — a spec containing an apostrophe would break, but paths don't have apostrophes typically.
- Note: `require ("../b/c.js")` is matched due to `\s*` — fine.

2. `requireSpecs` — fresh regex per call, good (avoids lastIndex issue).

3. `resolveRequire` — fromPath.split('/'), pop the file name... comment says "the requiring file's directory" but `pop()` removes the FILE NAME (last segment), leaving the directory. The comment is slightly wrong ("parts.pop(); // the requiring file's directory" — actually pops the file name, leaving the directory). Minor comment nit.

4. `normalizePath` — pops on '..' — if `out` is empty, `out.pop()` returns undefined, fine. A spec like `'../../../etc/passwd'` would climb out of zip root — but membership test would then check 'etc/passwd' which is not in the zip. No security issue (read-only classification).

5. `resolveRequireCandidates` — for spec starting with './', adds js/-root-relative candidate. But NOT for spec starting with '../'. Documented.

6. `unresolvedRequires` — checks `pathSetHas(paths, bases[b]) || pathSetHas(paths, bases[b] + '.js')`. Note that `resolveRequire` doesn't append `.js` if the spec omits it (e.g. `require('./common/helper')`). The + '.js' check covers that. Good.

But wait — there's a subtle issue: the knownPaths default builds `{}` from files' own paths — only files passed in. In the builder, `assertZipRequires` passes the full zip walk `paths` Set — includes non-.js files too (e.g. `manifest.json`, `launch.json`). Good.

7. Potential false-negative: `.js` files inside zip whose content is `source` read as utf8 — fine.

8. A subtle issue: the gate scans ALL .js files in the zip including e.g. `verdict.sh`? No — only `.js`. Launch extras like `verdict.sh` are shell, ignored. OK.

9. What about requires in `.json` files? Not scanned. Agent configs may embed JS strings in JSON? Hmm — pack zips contain agent config JSONs which may contain inline JS? The gate only scans `.js`. This is a gap but likely fine given dmtools compile embeds closure.

## Analysis of ci/pack_version_guard.cjs

1. `bump()` — `parseInt(parts[0], 10) || 0`. Fine.

2. `payloadFingerprint` — uses `manifest.files` — path + sha256. What if `files[i].path` is undefined? Would create 'undefined:hash'. Minor.

3. `fingerprintsDiffer` — null-safe.

## Analysis of ci/release_packs.mjs

Key flows:

1. `shippedCatalog()`:
```js
if (!PREV_TAG || DRY_RUN) return {}; // no previous release to read — ledger fallback
SHIPPED_DIR = mkdtempSync(...);
try {
  execSync(`gh release download ...`);
  SHIPPED_CATALOG = JSON.parse(readFileSync(...));
} catch (e) {
  console.warn(`::warning::...`);
  rmSync(SHIPPED_DIR, ...);
  SHIPPED_DIR = null;
  SHIPPED_CATALOG = {};
}
```
- If catalog.json downloaded but JSON.parse throws → SHIPPED_DIR not cleaned in catch (rmSync is in catch, actually the catch does rmSync(SHIPPED_DIR) — yes it does; wait: the catch sets `SHIPPED_CATALOG = {}` and rmSync(SHIPPED_DIR). OK it cleans. Actually look: catch block: warn, rmSync(SHIPPED_DIR...), SHIPPED_DIR=null, SHIPPED_CATALOG={}. Good.

2. `shippedZipManifest(agent, version)`:
```js
if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(SHIPPED_ZIP_MANIFESTS, key)) return ...;
if (!PREV_TAG || DRY_RUN || !SHIPPED_DIR) return null;
```
- Note: `SHIPPED_DIR` may be null if shippedCatalog() failed or was never called. In main(), `shippedCatalog()` is always called before (via `const shippedVersion = shippedCatalog()[agent] || null;`). If PREV_TAG && !DRY_RUN and gh succeeded, SHIPPED_DIR is set. OK.
- BUT: there's a bug candidate — in `buildPackRelease`, the drift check is only performed when `!isAffected && shippedVersion === next`. For an affected agent, next = bump(shipped) — never equals shippedVersion, so no drift check needed (version already bumped). Fine.

Wait — actually there's a subtle issue: `shippedZipManifest` downloads `${agent}-${version}.zip` from the previous release. But what if the previous release shipped the agent at a DIFFERENT version than `shippedVersion` (catalog says 0.1.36 but the zip asset name)? They should match by construction.

Another subtle issue: `shippedZipManifest` caches `null` results. Fine.

3. **Cache-poisoning issue in SHIPPED_DIR**: `gh release download --pattern '${agent}-${version}.zip' --dir SHIPPED_DIR --clobber`. `--pattern` uses glob. The agent name could be a prefix of another agent's name! E.g. agents `sm` and `sm_github`: pattern `sm-0.1.36.zip` — glob `sm-0.1.36.zip` matches only exact name `sm-0.1.36.zip` (glob has no wildcard here), fine.

4. **The drift-check skip for dry-run**: in dry-run, `shippedZipManifest` returns null → fingerprintsDiffer(null, ...) = false → no re-version. Dry-run is not published, fine.

5. **Critical check — the drift re-version path**: 
```js
if (!isAffected && shippedVersion === next &&
    fingerprintsDiffer(shippedZipManifest(agent, shippedVersion), zipManifestText(zip))) {
  next = resolveShipVersion(next, true);
  ...rebuild, gate, validate, return
}
assertZipRequires(zip);
```
- Issue: when the drift check runs, `shippedZipManifest()` is called BEFORE `zipManifestText(zip)`? Arguments evaluated left-to-right: `fingerprintsDiffer(shippedZipManifest(...), zipManifestText(zip))` — left operand first. OK.
- Note: For an UNAFFECTED agent, next = shippedVersion (base = shipped since unaffected). So `shippedVersion === next` is true whenever the shipped catalog has the agent. So every unaffected agent downloads its previous zip and compares fingerprints. That's ~68 agents → 68 gh download calls per release (lazily only when shippedVersion === next — which is every unaffected agent). Performance concern: each release makes ~68 sequential `gh release download` + `unzip -p` exec calls. Acceptable? It's a release pipeline, one per push to main. The PR description says "61/68 agents kept their version with byte-identical payloads" — so it works. Could be slow but OK. Maybe a SUGGESTION about parallelism. Not critical.

- **More important**: If the previous release didn't include the agent's zip (e.g. older releases only shipped affected agents — historical releases before the "build every agent" rule), `shippedZipManifest` returns null with a `::warning::`. Fine, degrades.

6. **The `versions[agent] = next` ledger write**: In main loop, `versions[agent] = next` for ALL agents (not just affected). And ledgerChanged check: `agents.some((a) => versions[a] !== (ledgerBefore[a] || '0.1.0'))`. If shipped catalog says 0.1.36 but ledger says 0.1.35, versions[agent] = 0.1.36 (base shipped, unaffected → keeps shipped) → l…

The drift re-version path has a real bug: the first-built zip (`<agent>-<shippedVersion>.zip`, with drifted content) is never removed from `dist/`, and the publish step uploads `dist/*.zip` — so the release still publishes a second, changed-content zip under the already-shipped version. arguments.content:
🚨 **BLOCKING: the re-versioned-away zip is still published — the release ships two different packs under the same version**

`buildPackRelease` builds the drifted pack at the *shipped* version first, and only afterwards decides to re-version. The first artifact (`<agent>-<shippedVersion>.zip` + its `.sha256` sidecar) is never deleted from `dist/`:

```js
const zip = buildPack(agent, next);            // dist/sm_github-0.1.36.zip (drifted content)
...
next = resolveShipVersion(next, true);         // re-version to 0.1.37
const rezipped = buildPack(agent, next);       // dist/sm_github-0.1.37.zip — 0.1.36.zip still on disk
```

The publish step then uploads everything in `dist/`:

```bash
gh release create "$tag" dist/*.zip dist/*.zip.sha256 dist/catalog.json
```

So even when the guard correctly re-versions, the release **still publishes a second `sm_github-0.1.36.zip` with different content** than the one the previous release shipped — the exact publication the ticket Goal forbids ("must never publish two different packs under the same version number") and the exact artifact class that poisoned version-keyed consumer caches in the incident. `catalog.json` points `@latest` at 0.1.37, but any consumer resolving `@0.1.36` against this release (or a version-keyed cache refreshing from its assets) gets the drifted bytes.

Fix — remove the stale artifacts before rebuilding:

```js
next = resolveShipVersion(next, true);
rmSync(zip, { force: true });
rmSync(`${zip}.sha256`, { force: true }); // `rmSync`/`basename` are already imported
```

(or build the drift-check copy into a scratch dir and only materialize the shipping name once the version is final). Please also add a wiring/level test asserting the re-version path leaves exactly one zip per agent in `dist/` — the current `gh-812` wiring suite checks call order but not the dist contents.
